title: Volume 2 Chapter 2: The Sister Cries, the Flames Do Not, and the Dagger Remains Unbroken 4
content: The full-body enhancement I had activated left my thoughts behind.
"Erika!"
Before the words could weave together in my mind, I shouted Erika's name.
The trust that unknowingly filled my voice was not betrayed.
"I'm not very good at protecting others, though."
The shimmering golden magical power informed me that my will had been conveyed.
I looked at Shara, enveloped in golden magic, and felt relief.
Now I could push Shara away without hesitation.
Shara, still wearing a clueless expression, was wrapped in the barrier created by Erika.
The excessive magical power contained within taught me that Erika's claim of not being good at this was not a lie.
She had overpowered efficiency and skill with sheer force.
"Don't bite your tongue!"
I warned her, thinking it was unlikely she would understand.
"Huh?"
Finally, a voice escaped Shara's throat.
Since we were in the forest, I thought I couldn't gain much distance, but I struck the barrier surrounding Shara with all my might.
"EEEEEEEE!"
Shara let out a scream that was hard to categorize, flying through the barrier.
In that moment, I took a breath.
As planned, I caught a glimpse of Shara soaring into the sky, weaving through the gaps between the trees, while I prepared for what truly needed to be prepared.
I gathered strength in both legs.
In my line of sight, I saw Erika, wrapped in the barrier.
What kind of expression is that?
What kind of face is she making?
I became aware of a warmth spreading deep within my chest.
For me, who had merely been chosen as a partner in this farce, to see Erika Solnzali making such a face.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/v6w0KbA.jpeg
Erika wore an expression of regret.
She seemed to be lamenting that she hadn't made it in time to protect me.
Her face was etched with a deep sense of remorse.
──Impact.
"My disciple really is terrible at magic."
I vividly remembered my master's exasperated voice.
"Yet, when it comes to magic that doesn't come from your own body, you're surprisingly skilled."
My master looked at me, who had channeled body enhancement into my sword, with genuine disbelief.
"And on top of that, you're absurdly dexterous."
My master scratched his head absentmindedly as he spoke.
This is it, disciple.
You should give up on ordinary magic and ordinary adventuring.
For now, just sharpen your skills; what you should aim for is...
Ah, here he goes again with his unreasonable demands.
"First, become the strongest swordsman in the ordinary sense."
There he goes again.
This person always easily applies his standards to others.
It's almost like──.
Just like Erika──.
──Erika!
How long had I been unconscious?
There was no need to worry about that.
Because I was still being blown through the air.
Ah, but I was sent flying straight up so beautifully.
And it hurt; it hurt more than I could have imagined.
What hurt the most was my arms.
I could only imagine what was happening inside my sleeves, but since I could see my fingers, they were probably still attached.
It was fortunate that they hadn't been torn off, even if it couldn't be helped.
After all, it was the price I paid for taking a direct hit from that thing.
I looked down at the monster standing in the center of the crater that had formed in the forest.
I thought I had absorbed about forty percent of the impact.
I gazed at the crater large enough to fit three houses from Hekatai and felt acutely aware of my own inadequacy.
The portion I couldn't absorb had been redirected, but the remaining force was certainly more than sixty percent.
In fact, I could say I was still alive because I had instinctively changed the direction in which I deflected it.
I wanted to absorb as much of the damage as possible to protect Erika, but my efforts were lacking.
This is what they call
"insufficient emotional capacity.
A man with insufficient emotional capacity is said to be disliked; I must do better.
I was slammed to the ground, unable to take a proper fall due to the pull of gravity.
As I crashed down, intense pain shot through my arms, which I hadn't managed to heal in time, but I ignored it and rolled away, slamming my arms into the ground.
I felt the bones in my arms break again under the sleeves.
But that was a trade worth making.
Just after I rolled away, a black arm pierced through the upturned earth.
That strike didn't have the flashiness of creating a crater, but it was filled with a deadly intent beyond measure.
As expected of the King series.
This is bad; I don't feel like I can win.
I looked up at the towering figure standing before me, feeling as if it were a miracle that I was even able to stand.
I wondered if the thought that had flashed through my mind—was a monster approaching that would cause the mid-level monsters to flee en masse?
The answer to that question.
The Great Demon Knight, the king of the monsters, or in more complex terms, the "royal species."
Oh no, this is bad. I might die.
The Great Demon, with black skin that seemed to be clad in armor, looked like a knight, hence the name Great Demon Knight.
It was a straightforward naming convention as always.
The names of monsters are absurdly simple so that even adventurers can understand them.
However, the Great Demon Knight is a monster that is rarely encountered, even in the Faltarl Kingdom, which is known for having powerful monsters.
In Faltarl, there is a clear difference between adventurer ranks six and seven.
Whether they fall within the realm of humanity or outside of it.
But the difference between ranks seven and eight is even greater.
That difference is measured by monsters known as the King series, like the Great Demon Knight.
Only when one can defeat them alone is one recognized as rank eight.
There are several types of such monsters, and adventurers who are still aware that they belong to the realm of humanity, meaning they are below rank six, refer to these monsters as the King series.
If one wishes to be recognized as having stepped outside the realm of humanity and even further beyond, they must bring back the head of a king.
But still, I see.
As I checked the condition of my arms, connected by the healing magic I was fully activating, I thought.
To call someone who can defeat this monster a human certainly feels strange.
I could only laugh at the overwhelming gap in power I felt.
The absurdity of feeling that there was no opening to draw my sword against a monster was nothing short of a joke.
The clear difference in power was almost scarier than my master.
Ah──, it's coming.
The speed of the giant, which was about fifty percent taller than me, was unimaginable.
The fist that was thrown at me appeared to me as nothing more than a blurred afterimage.
The only reason I managed to dodge was that the fist was imbued with magical power.
I recalled my master's words that some strong monsters use magic even to move their bodies.
For such monsters, the magic that moves their bodies activates before they actually move.
In other words, I, who could see magical power, could see the future movements of the monster illuminated by the light of its magic.
In less than a breath, I dodged three deadly punches.
Every part of my body ached; the cycle of my body breaking somewhere before the healing magic could fully take effect continued.
Regardless of the speed of the attacks, the frequency was manageable, which could be called fortunate, but there were no openings.
At this rate, I would be ground down.
Ah, damn it.
I decided to give up on one of my arms.
My left arm was crushed beneath my sleeves.
Using my left arm as a shield, I took advantage of the opponent's strength to create distance.
How simple it sounded when put into words.
With the distance gained at the cost of my left arm, I drew my sword with my uninjured right hand.
But that was as far as I got.
I was on the verge of collapsing from the intense pain.
My vision blurred, my clenched teeth creaked from the effort of not screaming, and my thoughts scattered in all directions.
Anger at the strength of the Great Demon Knight, fear of it, disappointment in my own inadequacy, and the pride of still being alive.
Anger at having my arm crushed, anger at myself for having to sacrifice it.
Ah, damn it.
My clothes were torn again.
A sudden, absurd thought crossed my mind, oddly calming me.
In this situation, my own frugality made me wonder just how deeply it was ingrained in me, and I almost smiled wryly.
In reality, I was still gritting my teeth in pain.
Thanks to that, I noticed something strange.
My left arm was still connected.
I had thought it would be shattered to pieces, but my left arm, though crushed and crumpled beneath my sleeves, was still there.
Yes, "beneath my sleeves."
I had braced myself for my enhanced arm to shatter, and ordinarily, my sleeves should have been blown away without a trace.
Before I could think about what had happened, I instinctively understood the answer.
"My frugality has reached its peak."
I muttered in a voice that, during body enhancement, could only be heard as a squeaky sound to ordinary ears.
To be able to use body enhancement not just on my sword but even on my clothes, my master would surely be exasperated.
It took me a breath to finally realize my frugality.
In the next moment, the magical power of the Great Demon Knight loomed before me.
The movements of the Great Demon Knight, where moving one's body equated to casting magic, were almost predictable for me, who could see magical power, at a level akin to foresight.
It was different from predicting movements based on the light of magic; it was the magic itself that traced the trajectory.
As far as I knew, most magic comes along the lines of magical power.
However, dealing with it was incredibly difficult.
Letting out a scream I couldn't even comprehend, I slid my sword into the path of the converging, certain death.
The moment the tip of my sword touched the magical power, I felt an unusual heaviness I had never experienced before.
It felt as if I were swinging my sword through heavy water.
Even without the opponent's speed, our own speed was insufficient.
I thought to myself, "Please, not now," as I desperately pushed my sword forward against the heavy resistance.
I spun my magical power within my body, feeling that even the magical breath escaping me was a waste.

As the fist of the Great Demon Knight, which looked like death itself, approached me with an afterimage, I felt something bend through my arm, and my sword slipped past the fist, leaving an oddly light sensation behind.
I had deflected the Great Demon Knight's fist.
In that moment of forgetfulness.
I could see the Great Demon Knight, who had been sent flying upward, losing its balance in disbelief.
In an abnormal situation where it had been lightly deflected by me, a being clearly weaker than itself.
The head of the Great Demon, which looked as if it wore a knight's helmet, instinctively tilted upward, following the deflected fist.
I was just as incredulous. I couldn't comprehend it, nor could I discern if it was real.
But my body moved.
My body, which had undergone countless repetitions of training that monsters lacked, ignored all the inexplicable.
The patterns that floated on the blade of my sword, enhanced by magic, seemed to be saying that it couldn't handle any more.
Before my mind could catch up, my body sought the maximum sharpness from the sword, and the sword responded.
This was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity; there was no time to hold back.
I thought that only after I had swung my sword.
The left arm of the Great Demon Knight flew off.
Hearing a roar that was neither a growl nor a scream from the Great Demon, what I felt was a deep sense of regret.
It didn't reach, my sword didn't reach.
The sword that was supposed to strike the heart of the Great Demon Knight, where the magical stone was said to be embedded, only severed its left arm at the shoulder.
I hadn't been fast enough.
The countless repetitions of training had not been enough to match the simple physical abilities of the monster.
The king of monsters, desperately avoiding my sword, was nothing less than a one-way ticket to suicide for its pride.
It roared out of frustration.
It roared out of fear.
It roared because it still didn't want to give up.
I crushed the part of me that wanted to be satisfied with having swung my sword with one arm.
I stepped forward to launch a counterattack against the Great Demon Knight, who was not in a perfect stance, but hurriedly halted my steps.
A dense line of magical power.
In a panic, I gripped my sword with my still-injured left hand.
The sharp pain made my eyes ache.
Desperately, I slid my sword into the thickest line of magical power.
The tip of my sword still felt strange resistance, but strangely, it was much lighter than before.
There was no time to ponder this strange sensation; all that remained was the sound of my sword parrying the fists of the Great Demon Knight, which fell like a torrential downpour.
There was no room for even a moment of thought.
In the span of a breath, I parried.
I felt a strange joy that the king of monsters had discarded its caution to defeat me.
In another breath, I parried again.
I felt a haughty anger at being underestimated as a weak creature by the king of monsters.
On the third breath, my thoughts began to catch up with my senses.
I started to understand the strange resistance transmitted from the tip of my sword and the sensation of bending something.
On the fourth breath, I realized that I was bending magical power, bending magic itself.
On the fifth breath, I thought to try cutting the magic, to try bending it significantly.
On the sixth breath, I could sense the king of monsters growing irritated and angry, and I found it amusing, yet I couldn't find an opening to counterattack.
On the seventh breath, I became aware that the magic circle of body enhancement I had been using at an intensity beyond my limits was about to collapse in about two more breaths.
I felt a sense of regret that if my body were sturdier, the strength of the magic circle could have been higher.
I had no intention of neglecting my efforts or training, but regret still arose.
On the eighth breath, my eyes and body began to catch up with the speed of the Great Demon Knight.
I crushed the satisfaction creeping up my back with my molars.
On the ninth breath, I suddenly realized that there was a body sturdier than my own.
Instead of giving in to despair because I was going to die, I was astonished that I still had the will to win, but there was no time left.
I was both astonished and amused at my foolish thoughts.
Oh, how enjoyable this is.
At the very last moment, as I tried to create a slight opening by channeling magical power, the magic circle within me shattered effortlessly.
Erika Solnzali was aware that she belonged to the category of geniuses.
In both swordsmanship and magic, she felt no discomfort being called a genius.
It was simply a fact that she was a genius.
And because she had talent, she hesitated not to hone it.
She could not understand the idea of letting something precious go to waste.
As a result, she gained solitude.
Though she felt lonely about it, Erika accepted it, thinking that it was just how things were.
Standing in the wilderness, it was not interesting to look back.
It was inevitable that the strong would gain solitude, as history showed.
Being treated better than being excluded was a small mercy.
While she desired conflict, the struggles of the nobility tended to turn into covert battles.
That was not to her liking.
At thirteen, Erika Solnzali accepted her solitude.
Because of this, when she met the Light Priestess, she wanted to help her.
She understood at a glance. This girl would soon find herself standing in the same wilderness as her.
So, Erika reached out to the Light Priestess.
To become friends.
Given their positions, it was unlikely they could stand side by side.
As time passed, their paths would likely diverge.
Knowing this, Erika became friends with the Light Priestess.
When standing in the wilderness, it would be more comfortable to have someone sharing the same wilderness nearby.
It would ease her loneliness to some extent.
And thus, she gained a close friend.
Erika bit her lower lip lightly. While being blown through the air.
It had been unfortunate that she had reflexively jumped backward.
The angle had been just right, causing her to be blown away with great force.
What a frustrating situation.
Erika bit her lower lip again. Regret burned in her chest.
She had not intended to neglect her magical training.
Yet, she was indeed poorer at casting barrier magic on others compared to others.
Because of that, she had not made it in time. She hadn't been able to cast barrier magic on Shin.
There were various excuses.
Prioritizing Shara's safety, Shin moving to distance himself from Shara.
The conviction that a medium strength would not suffice.
The time it took to infuse enough magical power for that.
But Erika could not forgive herself for those reasons.
What kind of genius was she?
A genius was supposed to crush and trample unreasonable things.
What kind of genius couldn't even handle this much?
In a fit of rage, true to her fiery Solnzali nature, she wanted to burn herself to ashes.
Even Erika, who was not an adventurer, could recognize that distinctive silhouette.
The Great Demon Knight, a monster known as part of the King series, a royal species.
In the academy's lessons, she had been taught that it was not shameful to flee from such a monster in a one-on-one situation against nobles.
She herself wasn't sure if she could win in a one-on-one battle.
With Shin by her side, she felt they wouldn't lose.
But at this rate... she would bite her lip off. Instead, Erika clenched her teeth.
Shin... Shin Longdagger. That person was fighting that thing alone.
Without hesitation, sacrificing himself to save Shara.
Would he be alright?
No, knowing him, he would certainly be fine.
There was no way he would die from something like that.
And then Erika realized.
I was──, protected.
She recalled the moment of the Great Demon Knight's strike.
Shin had stopped that blow with his crossed arms.
Why?
He shouldn't have had any trouble avoiding it.
Even if he dodged, he would still take damage.
But that didn't justify accepting a direct hit.
If that were the case, if that were true.
Erika remembered Shin's face.
The moment he took the blow from the Great Demon Knight.
That expression must have meant something.
But those eyes filled with determination were something else.
When was the last time someone protected her? Erika found herself confused by the long-lost emotion.
Her friendship with the Light Priestess was one of mutual support.
While they encouraged each other, they had never been in a relationship where they protected one another.
That was why they had been able to be such close friends. They had become friends by sharing the same wilderness.
But──, what about Shin?
Was he angry, exasperated? Or was he──.
Noticing her face growing warm, Erika panicked. No, this is wrong.
Feeling happy to be protected is unacceptable.
No matter how much Shin stood beside her as a fellow human being wielding only sword and body enhancement magic.
Feeling happy to be protected by the husband in a farce was unacceptable for a former marquis daughter.
Having never experienced being protected by a man of the same age, she was just a little confused.
Erika tried to tell herself that, but then she realized.
She realized it.
The difference between Shin and the Light Priestess.
That person... she understood now.
Shin stood "next to" her. A person who stood beside her in the same wilderness.
If that were the case, then there was no way Shin could die.
After all, he stood in the same wilderness as her, wielding only sword and body enhancement magic.
If that were true, he would surely protect the wife in the farce.
There was no way such a person could die. He wouldn't die from taking a hit from a royal species.
He was the only one. The only one who stood beside her in the wilderness.
He wouldn't die.
"Ah, but still..."
Erika unleashed her flames.
Why? Why was she not by his side when he needed her?
Shin wouldn't die.
But that didn't change the fact that she was anxious.
The explosive Solnzali could easily burn herself to ashes.
Even if she wished for the ground to come closer, it was still far away.
She envisioned Shin standing there, casually smiling at her in the same wilderness.
Would she lose him? Would she lose him?
"There should be limits to what can be taken."
Muttering a word in the air, Erika steeled herself.
Even if the world told her she was unwanted, she had no intention of being taken away.
"If I am a Solnzali who spills fire when I explode..."
She increased the strength of the barrier.
"Then I might as well blow myself away with magic."
Erika unleashed magic toward herself.
Almost vertically, Erika slammed herself down, breaking branches and trees as she crashed to the ground.
She miscalculated and couldn't land properly.
Indeed, it seemed she was quite panicked.
The impact brought a bit of calm back to her.
Next time, instead of casting magic on herself, she would push with wind magic or something.
As Erika thought this, she brushed off the leaves and branches tangled in her hair and used purification magic to remove the dirt from her clothes.
She couldn't go to help her husband looking like a mess. Even an explosive Solnzali cared about that much.
Ah, speaking of which──.
"I am not Solnzali right now; I am Erika Longdagger."
Though she had said it casually before, it felt strangely unsettling.
It was probably Shin's fault. Yes, it was Shin's fault.
With that conclusion, Erika started running.
